title: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays
byline: Liyin; Chen; Shengminjie; Miao; Ran; Huang; Zhiyi; Shan; Xiaohan; Zhang; Jialin; Sun; Xiaoming
html:
Abstract:Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realize maximum-weight independent set encoding on unit-disk graphs under the ideal blockade model, but embedding nonlocal interactions requires auxiliary atoms and limits the size of tractable instances. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, uniform cell weights guarantee that every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution of the original problem, even when local copies disagree. For binary quadratic objectives subject to pairwise Boolean constraints, every feasible optimum yields consistent active copies and a target weight given by an explicit constant offset minus the source objective. A rectangular variant of the architecture further encodes minimum set cover problem. Prior to constraint-induced site deletions, the full layout requires $2n^2 - n$ sites, halving the leading-order site count of a fixed complete-grid reference, while activity pruning yields an exact site count set by the propagation span. Across 18 paired benchmarks with independent ordering from a shared candidate pool, the layout reduces site counts by 12.1%-54.0%.
